constitution.title: รัฐธรรมนูญแห่งราชอาณาจักรไทย พุทธศักราช 2560 (Constitution of the Kingdom of Thailand, B.E. 2560, as amended)
constitution.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
constitution.note: Promulgated 6 April 2017 (Royal Gazette vol. 134 part 40 A). s. 83 (House of 500: 400 constituency and 100 party-list members since the first amendment of 2021; 350 and 150 before), s. 107 (Senate of 200 selected among candidates by group), s. 159 (Prime Minister chosen by the House), s. 166 (referendums), s. 252 (local councils elected; local executives elected or approved by the council), s. 256 (amendment), s. 269-272 (transitional appointed Senate of 250 and joint vote on the Prime Minister for the first five years). Not re-read here: krisdika.go.th reset the connection.

constitution_1997.title: รัฐธรรมนูญแห่งราชอาณาจักรไทย พุทธศักราช 2540 (Constitution of the Kingdom of Thailand, B.E. 2540)
constitution_1997.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
constitution_1997.note: Promulgated 11 October 1997: first directly elected Senate of 200 members by province for six years, non-partisan; party-list seats in the House from 2001; the independent Election Commission.

mp_act.title: พระราชบัญญัติประกอบรัฐธรรมนูญว่าด้วยการเลือกตั้งสมาชิกสภาผู้แทนราษฎร พ.ศ. 2561 (Organic Act on the Election of Members of the House of Representatives, B.E. 2561, as amended)
mp_act.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
mp_act.note: Constituencies, polling units (หน่วยเลือกตั้ง), the count at each polling unit and its posted sheet, consolidation by constituency, party-list allocation, and by-elections. Amended in 2021 for two ballots (400 constituencies and 100 party-list seats by largest remainder over the whole country).

senate_act.title: พระราชบัญญัติประกอบรัฐธรรมนูญว่าด้วยการได้มาซึ่งสมาชิกวุฒิสภา พ.ศ. 2561 (Organic Act on the Acquisition of Senators, B.E. 2561)
senate_act.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
senate_act.note: Candidates apply in one of 20 occupational and social groups and vote among themselves at district, provincial, and national level, within and then across groups, to select 200 senators for five years.

referendum_act.title: พระราชบัญญัติประกอบรัฐธรรมนูญว่าด้วยการออกเสียงประชามติ พ.ศ. 2564 (Organic Act on Referendums, B.E. 2564, as amended)
referendum_act.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
referendum_act.note: National referendums called by the Cabinet or required by the Constitution, held by the Election Commission; may be polled with a general election.

parties_act.title: พระราชบัญญัติประกอบรัฐธรรมนูญว่าด้วยพรรคการเมือง พ.ศ. 2560 (Organic Act on Political Parties, B.E. 2560, as amended)
parties_act.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
parties_act.note: Parties choose their constituency and list candidates through their own branches and members (the primary-vote provisions); the Election Commission does not run these votes.

local_election_act.title: พระราชบัญญัติการเลือกตั้งสมาชิกสภาท้องถิ่นหรือผู้บริหารท้องถิ่น พ.ศ. 2562 (Local Councils and Local Administrators Election Act, B.E. 2562)
local_election_act.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
local_election_act.note: Elections of the councils and executives of every local government (provincial administrative organizations, municipalities, subdistrict administrative organizations, Bangkok, and Pattaya), run by the Election Commission through provincial election directors; plurality in each ward or constituency, four-year terms, and a new election within 45 days of a term's end.

pao_act.title: พระราชบัญญัติองค์การบริหารส่วนจังหวัด พ.ศ. 2540 (Provincial Administrative Organization Act, B.E. 2540, as amended)
pao_act.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
pao_act.note: One provincial administrative organization per province outside Bangkok, with a council of 24 to 48 members elected by district-based constituencies and, since the third amendment of 2003, a directly elected president (นายกองค์การบริหารส่วนจังหวัด), each for four years.

municipality_act.title: พระราชบัญญัติเทศบาล พ.ศ. 2496 (Municipality Act, B.E. 2496, as amended)
municipality_act.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
municipality_act.note: Subdistrict (ตำบล), town (เมือง), and city (นคร) municipalities with councils of 12, 18, and 24 members elected in two, three, and four wards; the mayor directly elected since the amendment of 2003 (chosen by the council before). Municipalities have existed since the Municipal Organization Act of 1933.

sao_act.title: พระราชบัญญัติสภาตำบลและองค์การบริหารส่วนตำบล พ.ศ. 2537 (Tambon Council and Subdistrict Administrative Organization Act, B.E. 2537, as amended)
sao_act.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
sao_act.note: Subdistrict administrative organizations (องค์การบริหารส่วนตำบล) with a council elected by village and, since the amendment of 2003, a directly elected chief executive (นายก อบต.); tambon councils (สภาตำบล) where no SAO was formed.

bma_act.title: พระราชบัญญัติระเบียบบริหารราชการกรุงเทพมหานคร พ.ศ. 2528 (Bangkok Metropolitan Administration Act, B.E. 2528)
bma_act.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
bma_act.note: A directly elected Governor of Bangkok and Bangkok Metropolitan Council (one member per 100,000 residents of each district, at least one per district; 50 in 2022 and 2026), each for four years, and district councils (สภาเขต) of at least seven elected members per district.

pattaya_act.title: พระราชบัญญัติระเบียบบริหารราชการเมืองพัทยา พ.ศ. 2542 (Pattaya City Administration Act, B.E. 2542)
pattaya_act.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
pattaya_act.note: A directly elected Mayor of Pattaya and a council of 24 members elected in four constituencies, each for four years.

locality_act.title: พระราชบัญญัติลักษณะปกครองท้องที่ พระพุทธศักราช 2457 (Local Administration Act, B.E. 2457, as amended)
locality_act.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
locality_act.note: Each village (หมู่บ้าน) elects its headman (ผู้ใหญ่บ้าน) by the vote of its residents, and the tambon's voters elect its kamnan (กำนัน) from among the village headmen; both serve until age 60 since the amendment of 2008. The district office (อำเภอ) of the Department of Provincial Administration runs these votes, not the Election Commission.

local_direct_acts.title: พระราชบัญญัติว่าด้วยการลงคะแนนเสียงเพื่อถอดถอนสมาชิกสภาท้องถิ่นหรือผู้บริหารท้องถิ่น พ.ศ. 2542 and พระราชบัญญัติว่าด้วยการเข้าชื่อเสนอข้อบัญญัติท้องถิ่น (Local Recall Act, B.E. 2542, and the local referendum provisions)
local_direct_acts.publisher: Office of the Council of State (สำนักงานคณะกรรมการกฤษฎีกา)
local_direct_acts.note: Votes of a local electorate to remove a local council member or executive, and local referendums a local government may call on its own affairs.

dla_register.title: ข้อมูลพื้นฐาน อปท. (Register of local administrative organizations)
dla_register.publisher: Department of Local Administration, Ministry of Interior (กรมส่งเสริมการปกครองท้องถิ่น)
dla_register.note: Read on 2026-11-17 with searchCondition.pageSize=9000: 7,841 rows (province, district, local government): 76 อบจ., 35 เทศบาลนคร, 246 เทศบาลเมือง, 2,493 เทศบาลตำบล, 4,990 อบต., and เมืองพัทยา, in 76 provinces and 878 districts. Bangkok is not in the register.

dopa_stat.title: สถิติจำนวนเขตการปกครอง (Statistics of administrative units: provinces, districts, subdistricts, and villages)
dopa_stat.publisher: Department of Provincial Administration, Ministry of Interior (กรมการปกครอง)
dopa_stat.note: The Department's count at 31 December 2023: 76 provinces, 878 districts, 7,255 subdistricts (ตำบล), and 75,142 villages (หมู่บ้าน) outside Bangkok. stat.bora.dopa.go.th did not answer this environment (the gateway could not connect), so the figures are not re-read here.

bma.title: กรุงเทพมหานคร: 50 สำนักงานเขต (Bangkok Metropolitan Administration: the 50 district offices)
bma.publisher: Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (กรุงเทพมหานคร)
bma.note: Bangkok is divided into 50 districts (เขต) and 180 subdistricts (แขวง). www.bangkok.go.th answered HTTP 403 to this environment, so the count is not re-read here.

ect.title: สำนักงานคณะกรรมการการเลือกตั้ง (Office of the Election Commission of Thailand)
ect.publisher: Office of the Election Commission of Thailand
ect.note: Administers House, Senate, referendum, and local elections since 1998 (local elections since the Local Election Act of 2002) and publishes results. HTTP 403 to this environment on 2026-11-17.

parliament.title: สำนักงานเลขาธิการสภาผู้แทนราษฎร (Secretariat of the House of Representatives)
parliament.publisher: Secretariat of the House of Representatives
parliament.note: Records of the House since 1932, including the general elections from 15 November 1933 and the votes of the House on the Prime Minister. Answered HTTP 200 on 2026-11-17.

classes.note: 400 single-member constituencies by plurality since 2023 (350 in 2019, 400 in 2001 and 2005, 375 in 2011); multi-member constituencies with block voting by province or part of a province from 1937 to 1996 and in 2007. The House sits four years unless dissolved. The two annulled elections (2006, 2014) are listed with their dates.

cadence.locator: https://www.krisdika.go.th/ (Constitution of 2017: four-year term of the House from election day; a general election within 45 days of expiry or 45 to 60 days of a dissolution)
cadence.vacancy_rule: A vacant constituency seat is filled by a by-election within 45 days unless the House has less than 180 days to run; a vacant list seat passes to the next name on the party's list.

classes.name: การลงมติเลือกนายกรัฐมนตรี
classes.name_en: Vote of the House (with the Senate, 2019-2024) on the Prime Minister
classes.note: The House chooses the Prime Minister from the parties' declared candidates by a majority of its members (s. 159); the appointed Senate joined the vote for the first five years (s. 272). The King is head of state by hereditary succession and is not elected.
classes.disposition_reason: A recorded roll-call vote of the legislature, not an election by voters; the archive holds it as a parliamentary vote, not a contest.

classes.name: การเลือกตั้งสมาชิกพฤฒสภา
classes.name_en: Election of the Phruetthasapha (Senate) by an electoral college
classes.note: The 1946 Constitution's upper house of 80 members was elected once, in 1946, indirectly by an electoral college; the 1947 coup ended it, and later senates were appointed until 2000.
classes.disposition_reason: No official tally of the electoral college's vote located; the House Secretariat's records list the members chosen but not votes.

classes.name: สภาร่างรัฐธรรมนูญ
classes.note: The 1996-97 assembly's 76 provincial members were chosen by Parliament from ten candidates each province's applicants elected among themselves; the 2007 and 2015-16 drafters were appointed. The drafting process the 2026 referendum approved had no elected assembly by this census's date.
classes.disposition_reason: Members were chosen by Parliament or appointed, not elected by voters; a future elected assembly would be a new class.

classes.name: การสรรหาผู้สมัครของพรรคการเมือง
classes.disposition_reason: Parties select candidates through their own branches and members; no state-run nominating contest exists.

classes.name: การเลือกตั้งขององค์กรวิชาชีพและสหกรณ์
classes.name_en: Professional councils, cooperatives, and other non-territorial electorates
classes.disposition_reason: Elections of private or institutional electorates run by the bodies themselves, not public elections held by the Election Commission; the only state-run group-based vote, the Senate selection, is its own class.

classes.name: การเลือกตั้งนายกองค์การบริหารส่วนจังหวัด
classes.note: One directly elected president per province outside Bangkok for four years since the PAO Act's third amendment (2003); chosen by the council before. Terms were staggered by resignations until all 76 were elected on 20 December 2020; on 1 February 2025 the provinces whose president had served the full term voted, the rest having held early elections in 2024 after their presidents resigned.

classes.disposition_reason: Run by each district office of the Department of Provincial Administration as vacancies arise, with no central publication of results.

classes.disposition_reason: Run by each district office as vacancies arise, with no central publication of results; about 75,000 villages.
